{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Daniel Allcock''' is a mathematician specializing in [[group theory]], [[Lie theory]] and [[algebraic geometry]]. He is an emeritus professor of mathematics at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=https://www.ma.utexas.edu/users/allcock/prof/maximal_150921.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|accessdate=2018-02-11}}.</ref>

==Career==
Allcock graduated from the University of Texas in 1991 with a [[double major]] in mathematics and physics.<ref name="cv"/> He received his Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1996 under the supervision of [[Richard Borcherds]] and [[Andrew Casson]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=31501|title=Daniel Allcock}}</ref> After temporary positions at the [[University of Utah]] and [[Harvard University]], he returned to the University of Texas as a faculty member in 2002.<ref name="cv"/>

==Awards==
In 2012, Allcock became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>
